description: It is gone eight and the practical bench in the basement still has four boilers on it waiting for a qualified hand. The first-years have been here since the morning lecture, and nobody has eaten. On the shelf under the bench there is a tin of whale oil, a bag of barley, and a kettle that somebody has been using as a pan. There is a sense of hunger in the room.

options.label: Roll up your sleeves and make supper on the boiler you have just tested.

success.text: The first-years watched you take off your coat. Barley, salt, and a test boiler held at a steady simmer make something that is nearly porridge and very nearly stew. They eat it out of beakers. One of them says it is the best thing the Polytechnic has ever taught him, and writes your name in his notebook under the heading Pressure.

failure.text: Okay, you think, a boiler is only a big kettle. It is not. The barley welds itself to the plate and the plate to your thumb, and the first-years watch the player suck the burn in respectful silence.

options.label: Hand round two of your Rations and send them home before the boilers are tested.

success.text: They split two wax-paper bricks four ways, which is arithmetic the Polytechnic does not teach. The boilers will keep until morning. Most of them will.
